headline: Ajar adds an open-privilege measure to agent-defense evaluation
summary: A September 2026 preprint introduces Ajar, which measures whether an agent defense would allow tool calls that a task does not need, including calls the agent did not actually make. The authors attach it to AgentDojo and report that five defenses differ in how much privilege they leave available; attack success and benign task utility do not determine this measure, and a tighter defense can also refuse calls a task needs. This is a paper-reported result on one benchmark. The test labels, candidate-call construction and defense wrapper bound what the score establishes, and no independent reproduction was performed here.
